subject: Re: Evaluation MAP and credit/usage definitions for Zephyr pilot
messages:
From: Ellis Norwood <ellis@zephyr.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@zephyr.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 90-day eval and MAP for Zephyr pilot

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. We want to move quickly: a 90-day evaluation (pilot) with a mutual action plan (MAP) that spells out milestones for traffic ramp, committed credits, and an economics guardrail for true-ups and price protection.

High-level asks from our side:
- A clear definition of what counts as billable usage (tokens vs requests vs user sessions).
- A capped exposure during the pilot (monthly credit ceiling) with a true-up window if we overspend.
- Price protection for 6 months after pilot if we hit the committed ramp.

Can you share a draft MAP and the commercial terms you typically propose for pilots like this? Procurement/legal will need to see it; copying them here.

Cheers,
Ellis
Ellis Norwood
CPO, Zephyr.ai
ellis@zephyr.ai

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Norwood <ellis@zephyr.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 90-day eval and MAP for Zephyr pilot

Ellis — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a working MAP draft (MAP-Zephyr-Draft.pdf) and a short commercial summary. Key points summarized here so procurement/legal can review quickly:

1) Evaluation structure (90 days)
   - Initial free credits: 75k tokens equivalent (applied in first 30 days).
   - Committed ramp: if Zephyr moves beyond pilot, a staged commit of 250k tokens/month by month 4 (see ramp table in doc).

2) Billable definition (proposed)
   - Billable usage = generated tokens + incoming prompt tokens, measured at model invocation; we exclude logging/monitoring calls.
   - For multi-model routing we will apply the effective token rate per model as listed in the MAP attachment.

3) Exposure & true-up
   - Pilot credit ceiling: $15k/month. Any overage during the pilot is covered by a 30-day true-up invoice at the end of the pilot period (no automatic charge without procurement signoff).

4) Price protection
   - If Zephyr signs a committed contract within 180 days after pilot close and maintains the agreed ramp, Redwood will hold the effective per-token price (no upward repricing) for 6 months post-contract start.

I'll ask Legal for a short redlineable clause for the true-up and price-protection items — looping in laura.

Next steps:
- Laura to provide language we can share with Dana at Zephyr for redlines.
- Ben to confirm the credit application process in the console (how credits appear and expire).

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Dana Holt <dana.holt@zephyr.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellis Norwood <ellis@zephyr.ai>, procure@zephyr.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Zephyr redlines: true-up mechanics and usage defs

Karthik/Laura —

Thanks for the MAP draft. Our legal team reviewed; the core points are fine but we have specific redlines on two items that materially affect our economics:

1) "Billable usage" needs to be tightly defined. We can't accept a catch-all that gives Redwood latitude to reclassify requests mid-pilot. We propose: billable usage = tokens processed for customer-facing requests (production endpoints) only; test/dev and platform health checks are excluded.

2) True-up timing & limits: the 30-day true-up creates cashflow risk for us. We propose: any overage discovered during the pilot is eligible for a 90-day net invoice with a dispute window and an absolute cap equal to 150% of the monthly credit ceiling (so we can't be billed unlimited if there's a measurement error).

3) Price protection triggers: we want price protection to be triggered on delivered usage (not signed ramp commitment) so we are not penalized for delayed product integration. If delivered usage hits agreed threshold for two consecutive months within 180 days post-pilot, price protection applies.

Attached: Zephyr-Redlines-20260930.docx (redline comments inline).

Please respond with revised language we can agree to.

Regards,
Dana Holt
Senior Counsel — Zephyr.ai

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Holt <dana.holt@zephyr.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zephyr redlines: true-up mechanics and usage defs

Dana —

Appreciate the detailed redlines. We can bridge these items but need to preserve operational clarity for billing and abuse prevention. Below are compromise edits I put in a response redline (attached). Summary of the proposals:

- Billable usage: adopt your production-only carveout, with an exception: any endpoint flagged as "production" in the console will be billable, and Redwood will provide a usage export for audit. We will include an API to tag endpoints as non-billable for testing.

- True-up timing & cap: agree to extend the payment window to net-90 and a dispute window of 30 days from invoice. However, we cannot accept a unilateral 150% hard cap; instead we propose a cap for measurement-related adjustments of 150% but retain the ability to bill for bona fide customer-generated overages beyond that if supported by audit logs. We will include a simple escalation path to resolve discrepancies.

- Price protection trigger: we will accept delivered-usage-based trigger. The trigger will be: two consecutive months at >= 80% of the agreed ramp level (measured by billable tokens) within 180 days post-pilot. Once triggered, price protection lasts 6 months.

I've attached redline-response-20261001.pdf with the edited clauses. If Zephyr accepts, I'll instruct contracts to produce a short addendum that covers pilot economics and the MAP milestone table.

Operational note for Ben: please confirm how credits are applied and how we surface the "production" flag in the console so Ellis/procurement can see it.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Norwood <ellis@zephyr.ai>, Dana Holt <dana.holt@zephyr.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, procure@zephyr.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Final: MAP & pilot commercial summary (agreed points)

Ellis/Dana —

Thanks for the quick turns. Per the exchanges above, here is the agreed commercial summary we will include in the MAP addendum (we will circulate a one-page addendum and the updated MAP PDF for signature):

- Pilot length: 90 days; initial free credits = 75k tokens equivalent; pilot monthly credit ceiling = $15k.
- Billable usage: production endpoints only (endpoints can be flagged in the console as production or non-production; training/dev traffic excluded). Redwood will provide a usage export and an API to tag endpoints.
- True-up: any overage during the pilot will be invoiced net-90 with a 30-day dispute window. Measurement-related adjustments will be capped at 150% of the monthly credit ceiling; bona fide customer-driven overages beyond that may be invoiced following audit evidence and a short escalation path.
- Price protection: triggered by delivered usage — two consecutive months at >=80% of the agreed ramp within 180 days post-pilot. If triggered, Redwood will hold the then-effective per-token price for 6 months starting from contract commencement.

Attachments: MAP-Final-Agreement-20261003.pdf (draft addendum) — please review and confirm any final legal points by EOD Friday 2026-10-08 so procurement can process DocuSign next week.

Next steps:
- Zephyr: confirm acceptance of the four bullets above or propose a single final edit.
- Redwood: Contracts to produce addendum; Ben to confirm credit application and console flags; Marissa to schedule a handoff meeting with Customer Success for onboarding if pilot starts.

Appreciate the collaboration — excited to get this running.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
